issue_context.title: When ip_ban_enabled is true - will ban device IP that is setup as a trusted network and allowed to bypass login.
issue_context.body:

<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Have an Android tablet running Wallpanel - IP is set as a trusted network under auth_providers and has a user that is setup to bypass_login=true.  When ip_ban_enabled= true in http: section, it will ban the IP.  IP banned is 192.168.0.77 in this example.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 111.2
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): N/A 
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core):  Windows
- Integration causing this issue: N/A
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
homeassistant:
  packages: !include_dir_named packages
  auth_providers:
    - type: homeassistant
    - type: legacy_api_password
      api_password: !secret http_password
    - type: trusted_networks
      trusted_networks:
        - 192.168.0.76/32
        - 192.168.0.3/32
        - 192.168.0.77/32
      trusted_users:
        192.168.0.77: 16524566edc74125a7b0f4b47f24b4b2
      allow_bypass_login: true

http:
#  base_url: http://homeassistant.my-homedomain.org:8123
  server_port: 8123
  use_x_forwarded_for: true
  trusted_proxies:
    - 192.168.0.14
    - 192.168.0.77
    - 127.0.0.1
  ip_ban_enabled: true
  login_attempts_threshold: 5

```

## Traceback/Error logs

-->

```txt

```

@MarkHofmann11 I have not actively involved in home-assistant in last two years or so, but my memory said you cannot mix-use trusted proxies and trusted networks. 

Let me explain it a little bit.

`trusted-networks` is an authentication provider, if you access your system from your local network, you will be consider as authenticated user, home-assistant will assign an access token to your session. `trusted-networks` does not meant you can access home-assistant without valid access token, it just by-pass the user/password input phase, you still need token in your API request and/or UI access.

`trusted-proxies` is for which proxy allow to access your home-assistant instance, the allowed proxy suppose to have their own authentication and your have 100% trust to them. Put a proxy into this list, doesn't meant all request via this proxy will get access automatically, you still need go though login process to get access token, or use long-lived access token in your API request header
